_comment: Third-party ML-KEM implementations audited with --audit-kem, each pinned to
an exact commit, with the result pq-verify must reproduce. CI builds every
row and fails if pq-verify's result differs, so a failure means pq-verify
changed, never the library or the vectors (both are pinned).
Rows are only ever added. A newer library commit is a new row; the old row
stays, so the record shows when a library's behaviour changed.
AUDITS.md renders this table (python3 tools/vendor_audit.py --markdown) and
a test holds the two equal.
"edge" is per parameter set: the Wycheproof/CCTV edge-case stages of
pq_verify/edge.py (valid vectors, invalid eks, invalid dks).
dsa_audits: third-party ML-DSA implementations audited with --audit-dsa,
linked with pq_verify/harness/pqv_randombytes.c so their randomised APIs are
audited too. "results" and "not_applicable" are per parameter set. Each
mutant plants one known bug class in the pinned source; CI requires the audit
to fail it in every stage listed under "fails" ("rng": a randomness finding).
hbs_audits: LMS/HSS and XMSS libraries audited with --audit-hbs through a
pqv_hbs adapter (pq_verify/harness/hbs). One row per library: "results" are the
audit's stages, "not_applicable" what the library does not implement, "not_run"
key generation and signing over the default budget or sample. Mutants as above.
fndsa_audits: FN-DSA (Falcon) libraries audited with --audit-fndsa, DRAFT
TRACK ahead of FIPS 206. "results" and "not_applicable" per parameter set.
Signing is randomised and audited for validity, encoding and nonce reuse, so
the counts are fixed but the signatures are not. Mutants as above.
"accumulated" (per parameter set): pq_verify/accumulated.py, 10 000 seeded
cases hashed and compared with a pinned digest (Go's for ML-KEM, C2SP CCTV's for
ML-DSA); [1, 1] when the digest matches.
"ct" (ML-KEM rows, per parameter set): --constant-time, Encaps and Decaps under
Valgrind memcheck with the secret inputs marked; [1, 1] means no secret-dependent
branch or memory access. "ct_mutants" plant one leak each, with outputs left
correct; CI requires the constant-time stage to fail each in the stages named.
